identification.summary: Microsoft tracked DEV-0270, also known as Nemesis Kitten, as a sub-group of the Iranian activity group PHOSPHORUS and tied multiple ransomware campaigns to it [S1]. In an April 2023 update Microsoft renamed PHOSPHORUS to Mint Sandstorm and DEV-0270 to Storm-0270 [S1][S2]. Microsoft says the group scans the internet for vulnerable servers and devices and then encrypts victims with BitLocker or DiskCryptor [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft's profile was published 2022-09-07 [S1]; Secureworks reporting on the overlapping Cobalt Mirage cluster dates to May 2022 [S7][S8]. Earliest DEV-0270 activity is not stated in the sources reviewed.
identification.notes: Microsoft does not describe DEV-0270 as a front company in the profile, but says infrastructure overlaps tie it to two public aliases, Secnerd (secnerd[.]ir) and Lifeweb (lifeweb[.]ir), linked to Najee Technology Hooshmand in Karaj, Iran [S1]. Press coverage reports that Microsoft, Secureworks and Mandiant independently linked the activity to Najee Technology and Afkar System [S4]. Secureworks tracks Cobalt Mirage with two clusters; Cluster A (opportunistic BitLocker/DiskCryptor ransomware) corresponds in press coverage to the Nemesis Kitten/DEV-0270 activity, while Cluster B is a more targeted intelligence-gathering set [S7][S8]. Vendor cluster boundaries may not match exactly [S7].

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft assesses DEV-0270 operates on behalf of the Iranian government [S1]. Treasury (as reported) described Najee Technology and Afkar System as affiliated with the IRGC [S4].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft: moderate confidence that DEV-0270 conducts network operations, including widespread vulnerability scanning, on behalf of the Iranian government; low confidence that some ransomware attacks are 'moonlighting' for personal or company revenue, based on targeting that often lacked strategic value to the regime [S1].
attribution.basis: Microsoft infrastructure overlaps to Secnerd, Lifeweb and Najee Technology Hooshmand [S1]. Press coverage reports that OFAC sanctioned ten individuals and two entities in September 2022 [S4]. The Treasury release and the joint CISA/FBI/NSA advisory were not opened by this analyst.

objectives: Mixed or unclear. Microsoft describes opportunistic ransomware and data-extortion activity, including ransom demands (about USD 8,000 for decryption keys in one case) and offering a victim's stolen SQL database for sale after a refusal to pay [S1]. Microsoft assesses with low confidence that part of this is revenue-seeking moonlighting, while network operations such as vulnerability scanning are assessed as done for the Iranian government [S1].

targeting.notes: Microsoft describes targeting as opportunistic and often of little strategic value, driven by what vulnerable servers the actor finds [S1]. Secureworks coverage places Cobalt Mirage victims in Israel, the US, Europe and Australia [S8]. Parent group Mint Sandstorm is described by Microsoft as espionage-focused against dissidents, activists, defense industrial base, journalists, think tanks, universities and governments [S2].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through exploitation of internet-facing systems: Exchange (ProxyLogon CVEs 2021-26855, -26858, -26857, -27065) and Fortinet SSL VPN (CVE-2018-13379); Log4j exploitation was attempted but ransomware deployment was not observed from it; newly disclosed vulnerabilities are adopted quickly [S1]. Post-exploitation includes WDigest cleartext credential enablement, LSASS dumping via comsvcs.dll MiniDump (output named ssasl.dmp), a 'DefaultAccount' admin account for RDP, scheduled tasks pulling a renamed dllhost.exe reverse proxy, web shells, Defender real-time protection disabled, a spoofed root certificate, and Impacket WMIExec for lateral movement [S1]. Impact: a setup.bat script enables BitLocker, and DiskCryptor is dropped over RDP on workstations for full-drive encryption; ransom text is placed in the registry [S1]. Time to ransom was about two days in some cases [S1].

campaigns.name: Secureworks Cobalt Mirage ransomware reporting
campaigns.summary: Secureworks reported Cobalt Mirage ransomware operations using BitLocker and DiskCryptor, split into an opportunistic financially motivated Cluster A and a more targeted intelligence-oriented Cluster B; cited here as coverage of the Secureworks report.

campaigns.name: Microsoft profile of DEV-0270 ransomware operations
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes its profile tying ransomware campaigns to DEV-0270, a PHOSPHORUS sub-group, detailing Exchange and Fortinet exploitation, BitLocker and DiskCryptor use and links to Secnerd, Lifeweb and Najee Technology Hooshmand.

campaigns.name: US sanctions and joint advisory
campaigns.summary: As reported by The Record, OFAC sanctioned ten individuals and two entities (Najee Technology, Afkar System) tied to Iranian ransomware and malicious cyber activity, and the DOJ charged three individuals. The primary Treasury and DOJ documents were not opened.

campaigns.name: Microsoft renames actor
campaigns.summary: Microsoft updates its naming: PHOSPHORUS becomes Mint Sandstorm and DEV-0270 becomes Storm-0270.

diamond.adversary: Iran-linked operators; Microsoft assesses with moderate confidence they act on behalf of the Iranian government, with low-confidence possible moonlighting; infrastructure links to Najee Technology Hooshmand (Karaj) via Secnerd and Lifeweb [S1].
diamond.capability: Exploitation of Exchange and Fortinet SSL VPN flaws, LSASS credential dumping, Impacket WMIExec, RDP, web shells, BitLocker and DiskCryptor encryption [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Secnerd (secnerd[.]ir) and Lifeweb (lifeweb[.]ir) public aliases; reverse proxy masquerading as dllhost.exe; web shells on compromised servers. File hashes and IPs were not published in the Microsoft page [S1].
diamond.victim: Opportunistically selected organizations running vulnerable internet-facing Exchange or Fortinet systems [S1]; Secureworks coverage lists Israel, US, Europe and Australia [S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Unresolved mix of state tasking (vulnerability scanning for Iran) and possible private-company profit seeking, per Microsoft's moderate and low confidence assessments [S1]. US government actions treated the entities as IRGC-affiliated (as reported) [S4].
diamond.technology: Unpatched internet-facing Exchange and Fortinet SSL VPN appliances, weak local admin practices, and unprotected LSASS; built-in BitLocker and open-source DiskCryptor are abused for impact [S1].

gaps: Microsoft's profile lists no file hashes or IP indicators; IOCs are said to be in Microsoft products only [S1].

The joint CISA/FBI/NSA advisory and the Treasury press release were not reviewed; US government actions are known only via press coverage [S4], and whether the advisory names DEV-0270/Nemesis Kitten was not confirmed.

The original Secureworks Cobalt Mirage blog posts, Mandiant reporting and CrowdStrike reporting were not opened; vendor cluster mapping (Cobalt Mirage Cluster A vs B vs DEV-0270) rests on secondary coverage [S7][S8] and is inconsistent across outlets (some coverage equates Cluster B with Nemesis Kitten). No source reviewed stated CrowdStrike as the origin of the name Nemesis Kitten.
Sector-level victim data and total victim counts are not given in Microsoft's profile.
Activity after 2022 specific to Storm-0270 is not documented in the sources reviewed; the Mint Sandstorm page only notes the sub-group relationship [S2].
The alias UNC2448 and TunnelVision appear only in secondary coverage and are not firmly assigned to a vendor in the sources reviewed [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (battlespace): internet-facing Exchange servers, Fortinet SSL VPN appliances and RDP-reachable hosts on defended networks are the relevant key cyber terrain [S1]. STEP 2 (effects): ransomware via BitLocker/DiskCryptor can render hosts inoperable within roughly two days of access, and data may be offered for sale [S1]. STEP 3 (adversary evaluation): the actor scans broadly, adopts newly disclosed CVEs quickly, and uses living-off-the-land tools, Impacket WMIExec and RDP [S1]; its tasking mix is uncertain [S1]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is opportunistic exploitation of unpatched internet-facing services followed by credential dumping, lateral movement and disk encryption or extortion [S1]. MDCOA, labeled as analytic extrapolation, is that the same access is used for deliberate disruption of a defended mission network rather than for ransom; this is not demonstrated in the sources. Candidate indicators: new 'DefaultAccount' admin accounts, WDigest UseLogonCredential changes, comsvcs.dll MiniDump of LSASS, Defender real-time protection disabled, setup.bat enabling BitLocker, DiskCryptor drops, registry ransom text 'Your drives are Encrypted!' [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track patch status of Exchange and Fortinet systems and monitor for the Microsoft-listed behaviors above; ASR rules for LSASS theft and WMI/PsExec process creation are Microsoft-recommended mitigations [S1]. Authorities: response on DoD networks versus defense-industrial-base partners follows different authorities; this note does not resolve them. Mission assurance: offline backups, LAPS for local admin passwords, and restricting SMB/RPC and outbound connections from SSL VPN appliances limit blast radius [S1]. Coordination: share indicators with network defenders and the relevant government cyber agencies.

provenance.importedSummary: Microsoft threat intelligence teams have been tracking multiple ransomware campaigns and have tied these attacks to DEV-0270, also known as Nemesis Kitten, a sub-group of Iranian actor PHOSPHORUS. Microsoft assesses with moderate confidence that DEV-0270 conducts malicious network operations, including widespread vulnerability scanning, on behalf of the government of Iran.
